title: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
title_zh: 保护全球陆地脊椎动物免受未来海平面上升威胁
abstract: Sea level rise (SLR) threatens terrestrial biodiversity, yet its spatiotemporal and species-specific impacts remain unclear. Integrating relative SLR projections across five shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs) with area of habitat (AOH) maps for 34,120 terrestrial vertebrate species, we project that species exposed to SLR will increase from up to 13,680 in 2050 to 15,324 by 2100, including 57 to 63% of birds, 47 to 52% of mammals, 28 to 36% of reptiles, and 20 to 24% of amphibians. In Southeast Asia, inland inundation areas support high richness. Under SSP5-8.5, species facing >10% habitat inundation surge from 18 in 2050 to 109 by 2100, with reptiles and already threatened species overrepresented. Safeguarding SLR refugia—the noninundated habitats for exposed species—is critical, yet more than 96% lie outside protected areas, which means that early international action is required.
abstract_zh: 海平面上升（SLR）威胁陆地生物多样性，但其时空分布和物种特异性影响尚不清楚。将五个共享社会经济路径（SSPs）下的相对SLR预测与34,120种陆地脊椎动物的栖息地面积（AOH）图相结合，我们预测，到2050年，受SLR影响的物种将从最多13,680种增加到2100年的15,324种，其中包括57%至63%的鸟类、47%至52%的哺乳动物、28%至36%的爬行动物和20%至24%的两栖动物。在东南亚，内陆淹没区支持高物种多样性。根据SSP5-8.5情景，受>10%栖息地淹没影响的物种从2050年的18种激增至2100年的109种，其中爬行动物和已受威胁物种比例过高。保护SLR避难所——受影响物种的未被淹没栖息地——至关重要，但超过96%的避难所位于保护区之外，这意味着需要早期的国际行动。
